United States · Armed forces

RASP

Ranger Assessment and Selection Program

Illustrative training photograph

SELECTION TEST

At a glance

The U.S. Army lists a 12-mile ruck as part of RASP. It is one part of a longer selection process, alongside running, swimming and other activities.

FEATURED ACTIVITY12-mile ruck35 lb ruck · no time listed on current overview

What the test includes

  • 12-mile ruck with a 35 lb pack
  • Five-mile run under 40 minutes
  • 15 m swim in uniform
  • Other entry and selection activities

Some programmes include more than the activities listed here.

Test protocol and standards

RASP and the pre-RASP entry assessment are distinct stages. The public Army overview lists the following activities; it does not provide a complete administration manual.

Official information checked 2026-11-24. Confirm current requirements with the test publisher.

Stage / eventPublished requirementPractice context
Pre-RASP push-ups41 hand-release repetitionsUse the official movement standard
Pre-RASP plank2:35Hold a stable position
Pre-RASP run2 milesConfirm the applicable time with recruiting staff
Pre-RASP pull-ups6 repetitionsUse controlled full-range repetitions
RASP run5 miles in under 40 minApprox. 8.05 km; under 8 min/mile
RASP march12 miles, 35 lb ruckApprox. 19.3 km, 15.9 kg; time not stated on this overview
RASP swim15 m in uniformOnly practise under appropriate supervision

Scoring and scope

Do not substitute Ranger School standards, unofficial pack-weight definitions or internet time limits for current RASP instructions. Confirm the current selection instructions and packing list.

How to prepare

Independent training guidance, not official test instructions. Scale sessions to your current capacity and recover between demanding efforts.

  • Build unloaded running fitness and maintain a separate easy loaded walk. Increase distance, pace or load separately rather than all together.
  • Use longer steady walks on varied but familiar terrain. Record actual pack weight and practise foot care, pack adjustment and hydration.
  • Practise hand-release push-ups, pulling and trunk endurance with consistent technique. Use supervised pool practice for swimming.

Common mistakes

  • Running every loaded session; making heavy test-weight marches the default workout.
  • Confusing the entry assessment with the selection course or practising uniform swimming alone.

What to log

Track unloaded running times, pack weight, route distance, elapsed time, foot discomfort and recovery the next day.

Avoid repeated maximal tests and sudden load increases. Stop if pain, dizziness or unusual symptoms occur; use qualified supervision where appropriate.

Official test instructions

The organisation running the test is the best place to check the latest rules and requirements.
